title: SUMPRODUCT
explanation: A grocery receipt has quantities and prices. To get the total, you'd normally make a qty × price column, then SUM it. **SUMPRODUCT** does both in one formula: it multiplies two columns row by row, then adds up the results. It's also how you work out a weighted average, like a course grade.

tasks.prompt: In G2, work out the cart total in one formula: =SUMPRODUCT(C2:C8, D2:D8).
tasks.teach: **SUMPRODUCT(range1, range2)** multiplies the first cells together, then the second cells, and so on, and adds up all the results. The ranges must be the same size.
hints: The quantities are in C2:C8 and the prices in D2:D8.

tasks.prompt: In G3, work out the Produce total only: =SUMPRODUCT((B2:B8="Produce")*C2:C8*D2:D8).
tasks.teach: A comparison over a range gives TRUE or FALSE for each row, and in maths TRUE counts as **1** and FALSE as **0**. Multiplying by it keeps the Produce rows and zeroes out the rest.
hints: The comparison goes in brackets: (B2:B8="Produce"), then multiply by the 2 columns.

tasks.prompt: Last one: switch to the Grade sheet (tab at the bottom). In B7, work out the weighted course grade: =SUMPRODUCT(B2:B5, C2:C5).
tasks.teach: A **weighted average** counts some parts more than others. Here the final is worth 40% and participation only 10%. Score × weight for each part, added up, gives the grade. (The weights add up to 1, so there's no need to divide.)
hints: Click the Grade tab first. Scores are in B2:B5 and weights in C2:C5.

recap: SUMPRODUCT multiplies ranges row by row and adds up the results. Use it for totals, weighted averages, and conditional sums with (range="text").
